references.text: Aaron shall make atonement on the horns of the altar once a year with the blood of the sin offering. This refers to the annual atonement ritual performed on the altar, also described in Leviticus 16:18.
Blood shall be applied to the horns of the altar as part of the consecration ritual. This parallels the application of blood to the horns of the altar in Leviticus 16:18.
The description of the horns of the altar, which are to be made as one piece with the altar. These are the same horns upon which blood is applied in Leviticus 16:18.
The priest shall take some of the blood and apply it to the horns of the incense altar before the Lord. This is the same practice described in Leviticus 16:18.
Blood is applied to the horns of the altar that stands before the Lord. This reflects the same act of atonement found in Leviticus 16:18.
Moses took the blood and applied it to the horns of the altar all around to cleanse the altar. This is the same cleansing ritual performed on the Day of Atonement in Leviticus 16:18.
Ezekiel's vision of the future temple includes applying blood to the horns of the altar to cleanse it, reflecting the ritual in Leviticus 16:18.

The book of Hebrews describes how Moses sprinkled blood on the tabernacle and all the vessels used for service, stating that almost everything is cleansed with blood. This points back to the atonement rituals found in Leviticus 16:18.
